You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 80714b09bc574c5b23e50264e76e6e0f78d23549 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Vladimir Kondratiev <QCA_vkondrat@QCA.qualcomm.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2015 19:10:48 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] wil6210: fix format specifier for dma_addr_t

Fix format specifier used for dma_addr_t, namely use %pad
Debug print virtual address for the same buffer as well.

Fixes: dc16427bbe65 ("wil6210: Add pmc debug mechanism memory management")
Signed-off-by: Vladimir Kondratiev <qca_vkondrat@qca.qualcomm.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@qca.qualcomm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c b/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c
index 3cb4f35ebd05..8a8cdc61b25b 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c
@@ -92,9 +92,9 @@ void wil_pmc_alloc(struct wil6210_priv *wil,
 			GFP_KERNEL);
 
 	wil_dbg_misc(wil,
-		     "%s: allocated pring %p. %zd x %d = total %zd bytes\n",
+		     "%s: allocated pring %p => %pad. %zd x %d = total %zd bytes\n",
 		     __func__,
-		     (void *)pmc->pring_pa,
+		     pmc->pring_va, &pmc->pring_pa,
 		     sizeof(struct vring_tx_desc),
 		     num_descriptors,
 		     sizeof(struct vring_tx_desc) * num_descriptors);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c`**
   - The format specifier for printing the physical address (`pring_pa`) has been changed from `%p` to `%pad`. This change ensures that the address is printed correctly as a `dma_addr_t` type.
   - Additionally, the debug print statement has been modified to include the virtual address (`pring_va`) of the allocated buffer, providing more context in the debug output.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the format specifier from `%p` to `%pad` directly addresses the correct representation of the `dma_addr_t` type, which is crucial for accurate debugging and logging of memory addresses in the context of DMA operations.
- By adding the virtual address to the debug output, the patch enhances the debugging information available to developers, allowing them to correlate the virtual and physical addresses of the allocated memory more effectively. This relationship between the two modifications improves the overall clarity and utility of the debug logs.
